dz.headline: Bank ABC Algérie offers halal car loans up to 4.5 million DA
dz.dek: The Islamic finance product, Al Buraq Carousty, allows financing up to 90% of locally made or assembled vehicles.
paragraphs: Bank ABC Algérie has launched a halal car loan product, Al Buraq Carousty, through its Islamic finance window, Buraq. The financing can reach up to 4.5 million Algerian dinars for vehicles manufactured or assembled within Algeria.

This Mourabaha transaction, compliant with Islamic law, involves the bank purchasing the vehicle and reselling it to the client at a marked-up price, payable in installments over a maximum of five years. The loan covers up to 90% of the vehicle's cost and is available to salaried employees and retirees.

Bank ABC Algérie also offers other Islamic finance products, including "Moumkine" for furniture and "Alburaq Soukna Acquisition-Ijara" for real estate. These services are validated by a Sharia control committee composed of Islamic and economic specialists.

dz.headline: Algerian investor harvests apples 18 months after planting
dz.dek: Amine Derrar's 28-hectare farm in Tiaret yielded a good crop due to technical processes and irrigation.
paragraphs: Investor Amine Derrar has achieved a successful apple harvest on his 28-hectare farm in Tiaret, Algeria, just 18 months after planting began in June 2025. Derrar attributes the good yield to technical expertise, a drip irrigation system, and continuous learning about agricultural advancements. The farm's location at 1,000 meters altitude provides over 800 hours of cold annually, essential for apple tree dormancy and flowering, alongside ample sunshine.

Minister of Agriculture Sid Ali Khaldi visited Derrar's operation, which is connected to electricity and irrigation networks serving over 1,300 farms in the wilaya. This investment in Tiaret follows the success of apple cultivation in the Aurès region, inspiring other operators. Algeria produced 591,700 tonnes of apples in 2024 across nearly 32,000 hectares, with an average yield of 18.6 tonnes per hectare.

Algeria's apple production has grown by 27% between 2014 and 2024, according to FAOStat. High-quality apples can fetch up to 1,000 dinars per kilogram in Algiers. The favorable climate and increasing investor interest are driving this expansion in the fruit sector.

dz.headline: Algerian study finds link between eye floaters and retinal tears
dz.dek: A study of 896 people found 9.9% with posterior vitreous detachment also had retinal tears.
paragraphs: A study of 896 people in Algeria found that 89 individuals, or 9.9%, experienced retinal tears alongside posterior vitreous detachment.
Researchers also recorded 8 cases of retinal detachment and observed new tears in 3% of patients within two months who had no tears initially, according to pmc.
The findings highlight the importance of a retinal examination when new floaters appear, especially if accompanied by flashes of light or blurred vision.

dz.headline: Algerian author Yasmina Khadra calls Palestinian situation abominable
dz.dek: The acclaimed writer, participating in the Algiers International Book Fair, spoke about his new novel and his experiences.
paragraphs: Algerian author Yasmina Khadra described the situation of the Palestinian people as "abominable" and "unacceptable" during an interview at the 29th Algiers International Book Fair (SILA 2026). Khadra was present for the release of his new novel, "Le prieur de Bethléem," published by Casbah Editions.

The writer explained that his novel explores the dehumanization caused by violence and fanaticism, stating that fanaticism, not violence itself, strips individuals of their souls. He also mentioned being excluded by French literary institutions and juries since 2008, attributing this to unseen networks or lobbies.

Khadra encouraged young Algerian writers in Tamazight, Arabic, and French to persist in their vocation despite indifference and rejection. He advised them to write without expecting anything from others, as Algerian writers and artists often lack encouragement and face misunderstanding or censorship.

ao.headline: Angola becomes Ibero-American Community associate observer
ao.dek: The Community of Portuguese Language Countries congratulated Angola on achieving this new status at the XXX Ibero-American Summit.
paragraphs: Angola has officially gained associate observer status with the Ibero-American Community. This was formalized during the XXX Ibero-American Summit held in Madrid between November 3 and 5.

The Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP) congratulated Angola, stating the status recognizes its multilateral role and opens cooperation opportunities with Ibero-American nations. Portugal's Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel said Angola's accession brings Africa, Latin America, and Europe closer.

Portugal actively supported Angola's diplomatic effort. The CPLP, marking 30 years, includes Angola, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Equatorial Guinea, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Timor-Leste.

ao.headline: Angolan court clarifies insult laws
ao.dek: The Folha 8 newspaper explains the legal distinction between slander, libel, and insult.
paragraphs: Angolan legal experts are clarifying the definitions of slander, libel, and insult, often confused in legal cases. The Folha 8 newspaper detailed these distinctions on April 11, 2026, to help understand criminal imputability.

The newspaper highlighted that insult, defined in Article 213 of the Penal Code, targets an individual's intimacy. Examples provided include a former partner spreading rumors about someone's physical attributes on social media or a classmate mocking another's appearance.
These examples illustrate how insults affect personal dignity, even when based on suspicion. The Folha 8 report aimed to provide clarity on these specific legal concepts for public understanding.

ao.headline: Ebola kills 5,103 in DRCongo
ao.dek: The Democratic Republic of Congo's National Institute of Public Health reported 10,467 total cases.
paragraphs: The Democratic Republic of Congo's National Institute of Public Health (INSP) reported 5,103 deaths and 10,467 infections as of March 11, 2026. In the last 24 hours, 45 deaths and 53 new cases were documented. The current mortality rate stands at 48.8% for the neighboring nation.

Currently, 980 patients are hospitalized or in isolation, while 2,824 individuals have recovered and been discharged. The contact tracing rate is 86.6%. Eight provinces have been affected, with Ituri province remaining the epicenter, accounting for 70.8% of all infections across 67 of 178 health zones.

This epidemic is the deadliest in DRCongo's history, surpassing the 2018-2020 outbreak. Projections suggest it could exceed the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic, which saw 28,616 cases and 11,325 deaths in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Cases linked to the DRCongo situation have also been confirmed in Kenya and Nigeria.

ao.headline: Angola's sovereign fund buys stake in credit bureau
ao.dek: The Fundo Soberano de Angola will add a board member to Bureau, a private credit information company.
paragraphs: The Fundo Soberano de Angola (FSDEA) has become a shareholder in Bureau, a private company established to promote Angola's economic development. Bureau aims to reduce information asymmetry, minimize default rates, and promote financial education to improve access to credit for Angolans.

Bureau, legally established by Presidential Decree nº 275/20 and licensed by the Data Protection Agency, collects, processes, and analyzes financial and consumption behavior data. This information assists companies in making more rigorous credit decisions, potentially leading to lower interest rates and increased competition in the credit market.

The partnership, formalized through a subscription agreement on June 4, signifies a new phase of institutional consolidation and growth for Bureau. The inclusion of an FSDEA-designated administrator on Bureau's Board of Directors will strengthen its corporate governance.

bj.headline: Cotonou mayor orders cemetery upkeep
bj.dek: Luc Gnacadja inspects PK 14, Zogbo, and Akpakpa cemeteries after three months of maintenance work.
paragraphs: Cotonou Mayor Luc Gnacadja inspected several city cemeteries on October 21, 2026, including PK 14, Zogbo, and Akpakpa. The inspection followed his instructions from three months prior for maintenance work. The visit aimed to assess the cleanliness and improvements at these burial sites.

The mayor emphasized controlling service providers, standardizing grave preparation, and enhancing landscaping. He also recommended beautification efforts like tree planting. Gnacadja laid a wreath on a nameless grave on November 1, Toussaint, to symbolically honor the deceased.

The state of the Danto cemetery, with its overgrowth and lack of maintenance, was noted as particularly concerning. The report suggests that municipal authorities should regularly attend to cemeteries, not just before Toussaint, to ensure they remain clean and accessible.

bw.headline: Botswana nominates Gevorg Tamamyan for WHO top job
bw.dek: President Duma Boko cited the nation's health system challenges as a reason for backing the candidate for Director-General.
paragraphs: President Duma Boko has formally nominated Dr. Gevorg Tamamyan for the World Health Organization's Director-General position, with the appointment to be decided at the World Health Assembly in May 2027. Boko stated that Botswana's own health system struggles highlight the need for effective global health leadership, emphasizing access to healthcare and institutional effectiveness in his nomination letter to the WHO Executive Board chairperson.

Boko explained that Botswana supports a stronger WHO, not a weaker one, during a time when multilateral institutions face strain. He met Dr. Tamamyan and confirmed his commitment to underserved communities is genuine, leading to Botswana's endorsement. The President pledged that both Botswana and Tamamyan will adhere to the election's code of conduct.

Dr. Tamamyan is one of seven candidates announced by the WHO on October 29. A candidates' forum is scheduled for November 18-19 in Geneva. The Executive Board will select five candidates in early 2027, with the final appointment made by member states in May 2027, and the new Director-General taking office on August 16, 2027.

bw.headline: Stanbic launches P1.37 billion IPO on BSE
bw.dek: The bank offers 20 percent of its shares for sale, aiming for a 7 December 2026 listing.
paragraphs: Stanbic Bank Botswana has launched an Initial Public Offering (IPO) to sell 20 percent of its shares, valued at approximately P1.37 billion. The offer, which began on 30 October, involves up to 319.36 million shares priced at P4.30 each and is scheduled to close on 27 November.

This move by Stanbic signals a potential end to a nearly nine-year drought of new equity listings on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) since CA Sales Holdings listed in November 2017. The bank anticipates its Main Board listing on 7 December 2026.

Stanbic's IPO follows Kwa Nokeng Oil Holdings, which is set to list on 10 November after its offer was oversubscribed. Continental Reinsurance Holdings also has a P2.13 billion public offer with an expected listing on 10 December, making it a busy period for the BSE.

bw.headline: Botswana women's football faces funding gap
bw.dek: The launch of a 20-team Women's National First Division is threatened by a lack of sponsorship and infrastructure.
paragraphs: Botswana's women's football is growing, but a funding shortfall could halt progress. Clubs need more sponsorship and better playing facilities, according to Tsholofelo Setlhoko, Head of Women’s Football at the Botswana Football Association (BFA). The recent introduction of a 20-team Women’s National First Division, split into northern and southern conferences, provides a structured platform for more clubs and players.

Setlhoko stated that sustaining this development requires clubs to secure necessary resources. She met with African Club Association (ACA) representatives to explore support avenues. The BFA official highlighted challenges in sponsorships, infrastructure, and suitable playing environments for women players. Increased league size raises costs for transport, equipment, coaching, facilities, and player welfare.

The BFA president, Tariq Babitseng, who also leads COSAFA, has discussed a regional men's club tournament. Women's football already has regional club competitions that allow teams to compete beyond domestic leagues. Setlhoko believes these opportunities sharpen players' skills and raise the standard of play.

bw.headline: Botswana households spend 63% of income on debt
bw.dek: Bank of Botswana survey shows debt repayments absorb earnings as total household debt rose to P70.3 billion in 2025.
paragraphs: Botswana households are now dedicating 63 percent of their income to debt servicing, according to the Bank of Botswana’s 2025/26 Household Indebtedness Survey Report released on October 22, 2026. This high ratio reflects the pressure from rising borrowing costs, stagnant wages, and ongoing living expenses on consumers.

The survey found that total household debt grew by 2.5 percent to P70.3 billion in December 2025, representing 26.1 percent of the country's gross domestic product. While the central bank does not currently view this as a systemic threat, it noted that borrowers are increasingly vulnerable to financial shocks. Debt-to-income ratios for both men and women have risen, with those aged 40-49 facing the highest average ratio at 52.7 percent.

Signs of repayment stress are evident, as the average default rate reported by banks more than doubled from 2 percent in 2024 to 4.7 percent in 2025. The Bank of Botswana stated that household leverage has increased relative to income, reducing resilience to income, interest rate, and cost-of-living shocks.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso thanks Mali for hosting expelled gold miners
bf.dek: Minister Mahamadou Sana conveyed gratitude to Mali for assisting Burkinabè citizens expelled from Guinea.
paragraphs: Burkina Faso's Security Minister Mahamadou Sana expressed gratitude to Mali on Wednesday in Bamako for hosting Burkinabè gold miners expelled from Guinea. The minister, acting on behalf of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, met with his Malian counterpart, General Daoud Aly Mohammedine, to discuss the situation of these young miners. Sana thanked the Malian people and government for their support and care for the Burkinabè citizens.

The visit aimed to assess the condition of the expelled miners and arrange their safe and dignified return to Burkina Faso. Minister Sana conveyed the high authorities' concern for their citizens. Both ministers discussed measures to assist the miners and organize their secure repatriation to their families. This initiative highlights the solidarity between Burkina Faso and Mali, both members of the Sahel States Confederation (AES).

Around 200 buses have been mobilized in Ouagadougou to facilitate the return of these Burkinabè nationals. Transport companies have shown significant engagement, with many vehicles already en route or preparing to depart towards the Mali-Guinea border. This collective effort underscores the government's commitment to ensuring the dignity of its citizens abroad.

bf.headline: Prosecutor seeks 24-month jail term for lawyer
bf.dek: Ouagadougou prosecutor requests 2 million CFA francs fine for lawyer Ini Esther Doli for alleged defamation.
paragraphs: In Ouagadougou, prosecutors on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, requested a 24-month prison sentence and a 2 million CFA francs fine, all to be served strictly, against lawyer Ini Esther Doli. She is accused of alleged defamation against the municipal police of Ouagadougou in the case concerning the eviction of the "Allah Ti Kouma" establishment.

The proceedings were initiated by the commune of Ouagadougou following two Facebook posts by the lawyer on August 15, 2026. The commune's special delegation stated that her comments, suggesting that individuals involved in the eviction might be current or former clients, harmed the honor of municipal police officers. Doli denied targeting the police, stating her remarks were part of a broader reflection on prostitution.

The civil party requested a symbolic one CFA franc for damages, while the defense argued for acquittal, citing a lack of intent and connection. The court has set November 25, 2026, for its deliberation. The lawyer had previously been granted provisional liberty on September 30, 2026.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso launches patriotism conferences nationwide
bf.dek: Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala launched public talks on civics and patriotism in Kadiogo province on November 3, 2026.
paragraphs: Justice Minister Edasso Rodrigue Bayala officially launched public conferences on civics, citizenship, patriotic engagement, and peace culture in Burkina Faso's Kadiogo province on November 3, 2026. These conferences, an initiative of the ministry in charge of citizenship, aim to instill patriotism and civics in all 47 provinces. The talks also seek to bring populations closer to the ideals of the popular progressive revolution, including sovereignty and autonomy.

Minister Bayala delivered a message from President Ibrahim Traoré, urging citizens to cultivate sincere patriotism and responsible citizenship. He stated the conferences will reinforce citizen engagement against imperialism and terrorism, and promote community values for national development. The minister expressed a desire to see a "new Burkinabè" who loves their country and supports development initiatives.

The initiative is a collaboration between the ministry, the Presidential Initiative for Community Development, and the National Bureau of Major Projects. Similar events are occurring across the country, including the launch of the "Ligue de la souveraineté" in Fada N’Gourma on November 3, 2026, which aims to use football to develop young talent and promote social cohesion.

bf.headline: Burkina journalists trained on terrorism finance investigations
bf.dek: 30 journalists learned techniques for investigating illicit trafficking and funding of terrorism in Burkina Faso and the Sahel.
paragraphs: 30 Burkinabè journalists participated in a training workshop in Koudougou from October 27 to 30, 2026. The event, organized by the Norbert-Zongo National Press Cell (CENOZO) with support from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), focused on investigating illicit trafficking and the financing of terrorism.

The training aimed to enhance journalists' understanding of terrorism financing mechanisms in Burkina Faso and the Sahel, improve their investigative skills for illicit trades, and bolster their cybersecurity and source protection capabilities. Arnaud Ouédraogo, CENOZO coordinator, stated the goal was to equip journalists to better understand illicit economies fueling terrorist groups and to raise public awareness.

Participants learned about open-source intelligence tools, including satellite imagery analysis, and financial data collection techniques. Trainer Elza Sandrine Sawadogo emphasized the importance of identifying company ownership and real beneficiaries. Ignace Sossou covered cyberattack typologies and digital security for journalists.

bi.headline: Meheba refugees face new gate pass rules
bi.dek: Camp officials announced gate passes will now take one week to issue and last three months.
paragraphs: The new head of Meheba refugee camp in Zambia met with residents on November 4, 2026, to address security concerns. Issues discussed included difficulties obtaining exit permits, known as gate passes, stray animals, and a rise in banditry. Measures were announced to improve safety and community relations within the camp.

Refugees reported that delays in receiving gate passes hinder their movement, leading to arrests for lacking identity documents. The camp head committed to issuing gate passes within one week, extending their validity from one month to three months. Concerns were also raised about stray pigs destroying crops and dogs posing a biting risk, with owners given two weeks to regularize their animals or face potential culling.

The administration also addressed unauthorized construction and a reported increase in banditry. Residents were reminded to seek permission before building and to report suspicious individuals. The goal is to enhance security through better collaboration between residents and camp administration.

bi.headline: Burundi engineer disappears, three SOSUMO officials questioned
bi.dek: Ismaël Mugisha, an engineer at the Moso Sugar Company, has been missing since October 30, prompting an investigation.
paragraphs: Ismaël Mugisha, an engineer and deputy head of agricultural equipment maintenance at SOSUMO, disappeared on October 30 from his residence in Rutana province, southern Burundi. Three company officials, Arnaud Nikuze, Jean Claude Ntwari, and Aimé Clovis Irakoze, were questioned by the public prosecutor in Makamba on November 3 regarding his unexplained absence. Mugisha was last seen heading to work on the morning of October 30, stating he needed to complete biometric check-ins.

Mugisha, who had worked at SOSUMO for four years, reportedly had disagreements with management over equipment maintenance, advocating for repairs over new purchases. Internal sources suggest suspicions of mismanagement and potential fraud in equipment acquisition and upkeep, though these claims remain unproven by the justice system. Colleagues reported that Mugisha had expressed feeling threatened by some individuals within the company prior to his disappearance.

SOSUMO announced Mugisha's disappearance in local churches on November 1, two days after he went missing. The circumstances surrounding his vanishing remain unclear, with conflicting accounts from colleagues about whether he was seen at his office that morning. Heavy rains were reported in the region on the day he disappeared.

bi.headline: Burundi families sell land for stroke treatment
bi.dek: Stroke patients' relatives face financial ruin and disrupted lives due to costly care.
paragraphs: Stroke victims' families in Burundi are making significant sacrifices, including selling land, to cover medical expenses and caregiving responsibilities. Gisèle Kaneza, a student at the University of Burundi, has had her studies interrupted to care for her mother, who suffered a stroke. She is the eldest sibling and must manage household duties while her younger siblings attend secondary school.

Gérard Nibigira's wife is hospitalized after a second stroke, forcing him to sell their rural land to pay for her treatment and medication. The family has been at the hospital for nearly a month, highlighting the severe financial strain caused by the illness.

Stroke, also known as a cerebral attack, occurs when a brain blood vessel is blocked or ruptures, depriving brain tissue of oxygen. This medical emergency can lead to significant disabilities and destabilizes the economic and social well-being of entire families.

cm.dek: Cameroon's Deposits and Consignments Fund invested over 80% of its funds in government debt.
paragraphs: Cameroon's Deposits and Consignments Fund (CDEC) recorded CFA61.2 billion in securities transactions in the first nine months of 2026. Over 80% of these transactions involved securities issued by the Cameroonian government. CDEC aims to shift more than 20% of its investments outside government securities by the end of 2028.

The institution began investing in December 2024 with CFA9 billion in transactions, followed by CFA60 billion in 2025. These figures represent transaction volumes, not the value of securities CDEC currently holds. CDEC became a major institutional investor in government securities in 2025.
The CDEC's investment strategy is evolving as it becomes more active in the regional financial market. The fund's total transactions reached CFA61.2 billion between January and September 2026.

cm.headline: Governments accused of 86% impunity for journalist murders
cm.dek: UNESCO reports global impunity rate for journalist killings rose to 86% in 2026, a reversal of a downward trend since 2012.
paragraphs: The global impunity rate for journalist murders has climbed to 86% in 2026, according to UNESCO, meaning seven out of 10 killings go unpunished. This figure represents an increase of one point from previous years, reversing a decline that began in 2012 when the rate was 95%. Governments are accused of complicity and institutional failure in addressing these crimes.

The report criticizes governments for relying on excuses like conflict, terrorism, or insecurity to avoid prosecuting killers. It states that when journalists are killed, it silences whistleblowers and terrorizes newsrooms, ultimately blinding entire populations. The UNESCO report highlights that investigations are often dropped, judges are intimidated, or police are bribed, with powerful individuals like ministers or generals allegedly protecting perpetrators.

This high rate of impunity is described not as an accident but as a deliberate policy to send a message that speaking out carries fatal risks. The failure of justice systems and political courage is directly linked to the safety of all citizens, as the freedom of everyone is compromised when murderers of journalists are not brought to justice.

cf.headline: Central African Republic signs deals with Russia
cf.dek: Agreements cover communication, justice, transport, and energy sectors following Moscow summit.
paragraphs: The Central African Republic government announced on November 4, 2026, that it signed multiple accords and memorandums of understanding with Russia. These agreements, reached after the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow from October 25-30, 2026, span the communication, media, justice, transport, and energy sectors. The government views these commitments as opportunities to accelerate national development priorities.

During the summit, Central African Republic's President Faustin Archange Touadéra met with Russian President Vladimir Putin. They discussed economic cooperation and the implementation of agreements from the first session of the intergovernmental commission held in Bangui in September 2026. Russia reaffirmed its readiness to support the Central African Republic through investments and cooperation in education, health, agriculture, industry, economy, finance, digital, and media.

The Central African Republic government expressed satisfaction with Russia's approach to cooperation, which respects national sovereignty and strategic choices. This partnership aims to build a more productive economy, strengthen national capacities, and consolidate economic independence. Officials believe the summit results will usher in a new phase for Russia-Central African Republic relations.

cf.headline: Central African Republic distributes aid after floods
cf.dek: The Ministry of Humanitarian Action, with UNHCR support, provided essential kits to over 2,000 people displaced by heavy rains.
paragraphs: The Ministry of Humanitarian Action in the Central African Republic, supported by the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), distributed essential kits to flood victims in Bangui's 4th arrondissement. The aid followed torrential rains that inundated the capital and its surroundings, leaving over 2,000 people homeless and three dead. Beneficiaries received items such as tarpaulins, buckets, mats, cooking pots, and soap at the 4th arrondissement police station.

Minister of Humanitarian Action, Lina Josiane Bemakassoui, stated that efforts are underway to assist the displaced, acknowledging difficulties and calling for partner support. Residents like Wini Edoxie Yakona, whose home near the Ngouya Bagara canal was flooded, expressed gratitude for the assistance, noting previous instances where aid was promised but not delivered. The head of Dedengué 4 neighborhood, Dieudonné Ngofio, also thanked the government but urged for improved water drainage systems to prevent future floods.

Despite the current aid, flood victims report that their needs remain significant and are appealing for further support from authorities and benevolent individuals. Some residents contribute to the flooding by dumping waste into drainage canals, exacerbating the problem. The ministry is working to address the immediate crisis while residents and local leaders call for long-term solutions, including the construction of better water channels.

cf.headline: Police and students clash in Bangui
cf.dek: Tension erupts at Lycée des Martyrs after police attempt to arrest a student over a phone theft.
paragraphs: Violent clashes erupted on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, near the Lycée des Martyrs in Bangui, as police and students engaged in a stone-throwing battle. The confrontations, marked by gunshots in the air and crowd surges, disrupted parts of the Central African Republic's capital. Several students experiencing distress were taken to the community hospital.

The conflict began when police attempted to arrest a student at the Lycée des Martyrs for alleged phone theft. According to reports, the law enforcement officers did not adhere to proper procedures during the apprehension. Upon learning of the arrest, fellow students left their classes and headed to the police station to demand explanations.

The incident occurred near the Compagnie Nationale de Sécurité (CNS). The students' protest at the police station escalated into the wider confrontation that paralyzed traffic and caused chaos in the city.

cf.headline: CEMAC customs committees meet in Bangui
cf.dek: Experts from six member states are reviewing regulations to boost local production and cut import reliance.
paragraphs: Customs experts from the six member states of the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC) are meeting in Bangui from November 2 to 6, 2026. The technical meeting aims to establish regulatory foundations for a regional policy to reduce import dependency, strengthen local production, and enhance economic integration.

Seli Mbogo Ngabo, CEMAC Commissioner for the Common Market, opened the meeting, emphasizing the committees' role in harmonizing customs and fiscal regulations. The experts are examining conclusions from a July workshop in Brazzaville on implementing the regional import-substitution strategy adopted in March 2023. This strategy targets local production of rice, cassava, wheat, beef, and fish to decrease structural reliance on imports.

The strategy seeks to stimulate local output, reinforce regional value chains, and limit foreign currency outflows for food imports. The Bangui session will determine regulatory mechanisms for the effective application of these recommendations.

km.headline: Comoros notaries train to fight money laundering
km.dek: A national training session on detecting suspicious funds precedes professional immersion for notaries in Reunion and Mayotte.
paragraphs: The Comoros National Chamber of Notaries held a training session on October 31 focused on combating money laundering and terrorist financing. This event prepares notaries for upcoming professional immersion programs in La Réunion and Mayotte. The training covered identifying beneficial owners, vigilance towards politically exposed persons, detecting suspicious operations, and reporting procedures.

This initiative, organized with the Chamber of Notaries of La Réunion, aims to align Comorian notarial practices with Financial Action Task Force (GAFI) standards. The session was co-led by Anne-Françoise Zattara, a professor at the University of La Réunion, and Ait Ahmed Mohamed Djalim, secretary general of the Comorian Financial Intelligence Service. Notaries are involved in real estate and asset transactions that could be used for funds of dubious origin.

Following the training, the presidents of the two chambers signed agreements on November 2 for the upcoming immersion stages. Notaries will soon join practices in La Réunion and Mayotte to enhance their practical skills. The training lasted three hours and focused on four key areas.

cg.headline: Congo launches energy study for special economic zones
cg.dek: The study, launched November 3, 2026, aims to secure energy supplies for industrial zones by 2030.
paragraphs: The Republic of Congo officially launched a study on November 3, 2026, in Brazzaville to secure energy supplies for its future industrial zones by 2030. The Ministry of Energy is overseeing the initiative, implemented by the National Agency for Rural Electrification with support from the UN Development Programme. This study will assess the energy needs of various industrial zones and identify suitable solutions, including solar power with storage, biomass, and grid connections.

Minister Michel Djombo stated that the study aims to strengthen electrification for Special Economic Zones (ZES). The goal is to propose reliable, sustainable, and economically viable energy solutions to meet industrial demands. Ensuring sufficient and regular energy is essential for attracting investors, developing production units, and processing raw materials locally.

This effort is part of the National Energy Pact and the international Mission 300 initiative. It seeks to identify projects for public and private funding, balancing industrial development with the energy transition and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. Expected outcomes include job creation, local value chain development, and strengthening the national production base by 2030.

cg.headline: Congo launches third phase of HeSP health security program
cg.dek: Nearly 180 participants gathered in Brazzaville for the regional meeting on strengthening health security.
paragraphs: Prime Minister Anatole Collinet Makosso officially launched the third phase of the Health Security Programme in West and Central Africa (HeSP) in Brazzaville on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The launch took place during a regional conference focused on sharing knowledge and experiences among participating countries, with nearly 180 representatives from states, regional institutions, and international partners in attendance.

This phase of the HeSP program involves Congo, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, and Chad. Its aim is to strengthen cooperation mechanisms between these nations, improve epidemiological surveillance, and enhance national capacities for preventing and responding to health emergencies. The participating states intend to better anticipate health risks and coordinate their responses to epidemics and other threats that could cross borders.

The program seeks to foster collective responses and more effective monitoring systems for countries facing shared health challenges. Prime Minister Makosso stated that Africa is committed to uniting its forces to effectively combat epidemics.

cg.headline: Congolese novel published after 50 years
cg.dek: Jean Malonga's 'Cœur d'Aryenne', written in 1953, is now available from Présence Africaine.
paragraphs: Jean Malonga's first novel from Brazzaville, 'Cœur d'Aryenne', has been published by Présence Africaine more than 50 years after it was written.

The novel, set in Mossaka in the Republic of Congo, tells the story of a young Congolese boy named Mambeke who saves the daughter of white colonists from drowning. The story explores themes of colonialism and racial ideology, drawing parallels to historical debates about the humanity of indigenous peoples.
The book was previously only accessible in specialized libraries. The narrative begins with Mambeke rescuing Solange, the daughter of colonist Roch Morax, from a caiman in the river.

paragraphs: Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara met with French President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, for discussions at the Élysée Palace. The press review also noted other news, including US midterm election results where Donald Trump reportedly faced a "stinging setback." Nationally, rumors of a ministerial reshuffle were circulating, with Le Jour Plus reporting that "the noise is growing, growing, growing!" The Ivorian bar association's stance on distinguishing political protest from terrorism was also a topic, with Le Temps stating "the bar refuses to equate political protest with terrorism."

ci.headline: Ivory Coast trains rice processors to boost local quality
ci.dek: A four-day workshop in Yamoussoukro aims to improve milled rice quality and competitiveness against imports.
paragraphs: The Agency for the Development of the Rice Sector (ADERIZ), through the REWARD-CI project, organized a four-day capacity-building workshop in Yamoussoukro starting November 4, 2026. The training targets managers of mini rice mills, processing one to two tons per hour, to enhance the quality of local milled rice and its competitiveness against imports.

According to Brou Jérémy Kouadio, technical operations chief for REWARD-CI, the initiative addresses paddy supply shortages, quality issues, and inadequate equipment. Upon completion, participants will better understand their equipment's operation and how to improve rice quality to meet market demands. A diagnostic mission will follow to identify specific needs for factory upgrades and environmental compliance, facilitating bank financing.

The REWARD-CI project, launched in June 2026 and ending April 2028, aims to strengthen food sovereignty in West Africa by providing quality milled rice and increasing private investment. The project is active in seven to eight regions of Ivory Coast and is part of a national strategy to make rice a competitive sector by 2030.

ci.headline: Abidjan hosts second vascular surgery mission
ci.dek: French and Ivorian medical teams treated four patients for vascular diseases between October 26 and 28.
paragraphs: The Institut Cœur de Grâce (ICG) in Abidjan held its second vascular surgery mission from October 26 to 28, 2026. The mission, part of a collaboration with French specialized hospitals, aimed to combat cardiovascular diseases in Ivory Coast.

Led by French vascular surgeon Dr. Aurélien Besancenot and including ICG specialist Dr. Séka Antoine, the team examined four patients. Three patients with lower limb arterial disease underwent procedures like angioplasty and a right carotid operation.

Dr. Besancenot highlighted the growing public health challenge of vascular diseases due to aging populations and obesity. ICG's scientific director, Professor Iklo Coulibaly, praised the mission for advancing specialized care and improving access to treatment in Ivory Coast.

eg.headline: Egypt raises $500 million from dollar bonds
eg.dek: The Finance Ministry sold additional bonds maturing in 2030 and 2033 to diversify funding.
paragraphs: Egypt raised USD 500 million on Tuesday by selling more bonds under two existing dollar issues, according to the Finance Ministry. The sale added USD 150 million to a bond maturing in 2030 and USD 350 million to one maturing in 2033. This reopening strategy allows the government to raise funds without creating new securities.

The Finance Ministry stated the sale is part of a plan to diversify funding tools and markets, attract new investor types, and extend the average maturity of Egypt's debt. The ministry noted the sale proceeded despite global economic challenges, geopolitical tensions, and increased uncertainty.

The ministry renewed its commitment to reducing external debt for state budget entities by USD 1 billion to USD 2 billion annually through greater repayment than borrowing abroad. In the last fiscal year, this debt was reduced by approximately USD 2.4 billion.

eg.headline: Egypt targets 100,000 electric vehicles by 2032
eg.dek: Government plans to boost local manufacturing and reduce import dependence for automotive components.
paragraphs: Egypt aims to produce up to 100,000 electric vehicles annually by 2032, a move designed to cut import reliance and boost domestic manufacturing. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reviewed the government's plan to localize the automotive industry, emphasizing its importance for industrial growth and export potential to neighboring markets.

Industry Minister Khaled Hashem detailed partnerships to increase local production of automotive components, including an agreement for 8 million metal parts annually. A vocational school for mould and die manufacturing is also planned. Discussions are underway for local battery supply for buses and vehicles, and for electric motors.

A major international automaker plans to start producing three electric vehicle models in Egypt in 2027, targeting 100,000 vehicles annually by 2032. This company aims to increase local component content from 10% to 27% by 2032. China's Dongfeng has already begun electric vehicle manufacturing in partnership with SN Automotive and El Nasr Automotive.

eg.headline: Egypt seeks port integration with Slovenia
eg.dek: Cairo also wants a labour migration pact to send Egyptian workers to meet Slovenian demand.
paragraphs: Egypt aims to connect its national seaports with Slovenia’s Port of Koper and secure a labour migration agreement for Egyptian workers, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly announced on Wednesday. Madbouly proposed expanding cooperation between the Port of Alexandria and the Port of Koper to include Egypt’s Ain Sokhna and Damietta ports. This integration seeks to boost Egyptian exports to the European Union and aid Slovenia’s access to African markets.

The discussions occurred during a meeting with Slovenian President Nataša Pirc Musar in Cairo, coinciding with an economic event featuring a 25-company Slovenian trade delegation. Madbouly stated Egypt's intention to formalise a labour migration agreement to supply workers for sectors Slovenia prioritises. He also outlined Egypt’s energy infrastructure plans, including an electricity interconnection with Greece and linking Cypriot gas fields to Egyptian facilities.

President Pirc Musar identified the automotive industry as a key area for expansion, with Egypt prioritising localised electric vehicle production. Cooperation opportunities were also noted in tourism and sciences like artificial intelligence. Madbouly proposed sending Egyptian students to Slovenian institutions, citing existing ties between Cairo University and the University of Ljubljana.

eg.headline: Egypt MP proposes end to leniency in honour killings
eg.dek: Fatma Adel's draft bill seeks tougher penalties for rape and sexual assault, removing honour as a defence.
paragraphs: Member of Parliament Fatma Adel has introduced a draft bill to amend Egypt’s Penal Code, Law No. 58 of 1937, aiming to end leniency in honour killings and sexual violence cases. The proposed legislation seeks to classify killings of a spouse or former spouse, or someone caught committing adultery with a spouse, as premeditated murder. It would also prevent judges from reducing sentences based on surprise, revenge, family honour, or social circumstances.

Adel, representing the Justice Party, stated the bill addresses the role of law in protecting victims of violence against women. The proposal challenges deeply rooted social attitudes by questioning whether cultural expectations or family reputation should ever justify violence. The draft bill aims to introduce tougher penalties for rape and sexual assault.

The proposed amendment to the Penal Code has reignited debate about violence against women. The legislation seeks to restrict the circumstances in which judges can reduce sentences for serious offences. This move directly impacts the legal framework surrounding crimes of passion and sexual assault within Egypt.

gq.headline: Prosecutor seeks life sentence for sergeant accused of murder
gq.dek: The military court in Micomeseng heard charges against Sergeant Rafael Edjang Edjo for allegedly killing two women.
paragraphs: A military court in Micomeseng has heard the case against Sergeant Rafael Edjang Edjo, who is accused of murdering two women at the Meban Nkan military facility. The prosecution is seeking a life sentence for Edjang.

The court, presided over by Rear Admiral Tiburcio Ngomo Ndong, also considered the case of Corporal Juan Pablo Obiang Ndong, who faces charges of abandonment of service, fraud, and disobedience. The prosecution requested four years in prison and permanent dismissal for Obiang Ndong, who was allegedly asleep and intoxicated during the incident. The Ministry of Defence was also asked to arrange compensation for the victims' families.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea reviews Securiport border control fees
gq.dek: Vice President Nguema Obiang Mangue chairs meeting in Malabo to assess company's economic proposal.
paragraphs: Equatorial Guinea's government reviewed Securiport's economic proposal for border control modernization in Malabo on Tuesday. Vice President Nguema Obiang Mangue led the meeting, attended by the prime minister and ministers of Transport, Security, and Finance. The group examined the fees and services offered by the U.S. company, which previously operated in the country.

Obiang Mangue requested a comparison of current and past contract conditions to ensure new fees align with planned services. He stressed that the project must meet national needs without unnecessary expenses that could burden passengers or deter tourism. A pilot phase at Malabo and Bata airports is recommended to test the system's effectiveness before wider implementation.

Securiport first proposed modernizing airport security in November 2025. Authorities are negotiating financial terms to enhance border controls and traveler safety without imposing undue costs on the state or citizens. The goal is to strengthen security at all national airports, ports, and border crossings.

The institute also provides services including a library, children's Saturdays, dance workshops, and film screenings. The celebration reaffirmed the ICEF's role as a center for training and cultural exchange.

er.headline: US lifts sanctions on Eritrea
er.dek: Sanctions removed on September 19, 2026, targeted the ruling party's financial and military apparatus.
paragraphs: The United States removed sanctions on Eritrea on September 19, 2026. These sanctions were imposed in 2021 due to Eritrea’s involvement in the Tigray War. The US government had outlined plans to lift the sanctions four months prior, according to a Reuters report.

Human rights groups criticized the decision, citing Eritrea's record of forced labor and torture under the ruling People’s Front for Democracy and Justice (PFDJ). Eritrea's government called the sanctions 'illicit and immoral' and claimed they caused 'incalculable damage' and constrained development.

The removed sanctions targeted the PFDJ’s financial and military bodies and two officials, Abraha Kassa and Hagos Gebrehiwet. The Eritrean Defence Force’s chief of staff, Filipos Woldeyohannes, remains under separate sanctions. The PFDJ has previously benefited from the removal of UN sanctions in 2018, remaining self-sufficient.

ke.headline: Wetangula, Kingi lead MPs to visit recuperating Oburu
ke.dek: National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetangula and Senate Speaker Amason Kingi visited ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi home on November 5.
paragraphs: National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetangula and Senate Speaker Amason Kingi visited Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Party Leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi home on November 5. They led a delegation of MPs and Senators to wish the Siaya Senator a speedy recovery after his discharge from hospital.

Wetangula advised Oburu to prioritize his health and avoid rushing back to political engagements, commending his courage. Oburu expressed gratitude for the visit, stating that false social media reports declaring him dead while hospitalized had only strengthened his resolve. "Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness," he said.

Oburu acknowledged his illness had temporarily slowed his political activities but vowed to return to parliamentary debates and active discourse soon. Senate Speaker Kingi noted that the Senate fraternity missed Oburu’s contributions to proceedings and national politics. The delegation included Senators David Wakoli, Stewart Madzayo, William Kisang, and Daniel Maanzo, alongside MPs Millie Odhiambo, Mishi Mboko, and Eve Obara.

ke.headline: Kenya macadamia crisis: 30,000 tonnes unsold
ke.dek: Only 5% of expected macadamia nuts shipped before export window closed, leaving farmers and processors facing losses.
paragraphs: More than 30,000 metric tons of raw macadamia nuts remain unsold in Kenya after the export window closed on October 10. The Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA) reported that only 700 metric tons of the expected 14,000 metric tons were shipped before the deadline. This leaves processors and farmers counting significant losses due to the unexported allocation.

Industry stakeholders attribute the low export volume to bureaucratic hurdles and strict deadlines, preventing farmers from accessing international markets and improving farmgate prices. Kenya Macadamia Growers Association Vice Chairman Mureithi Gichabi urged the government to extend the export period, faulting the regulator for not facilitating the process. Nut Traders Association of Kenya Vice Chairman Njiru Kathangu called for predictable policies, including lifting the ban on raw nut exports to China.

Macadamia value chain expert Peter Mwangi warned the current crisis mirrors a similar situation three years ago. In Nakuru, large-estate representative Jacinta Mwai reported over 5,000 metric tons awaiting shipment, citing damage to investor confidence from policy uncertainty. A farmer in Murang’a, Jane Wambui, noted the glut has weakened farmers’ bargaining power, leading to low farmgate prices.

ke.headline: Njeru Ndwiga appointed Kenya Coffee Board chairperson
ke.dek: Henry Kinyua will lead the Coffee Research and Training Institute as the sector aims to boost annual production to 150,000 metric tonnes.
paragraphs: Njeru Peter Ndwiga began a three-year term as the Non-Executive Chairperson of the Coffee Board of Kenya on October 30, 2026. President William Ruto made the appointment via Gazette Notice No. 16957, replacing Henry Gihuhi Kinyua.

Ndwiga, a former Embu Senator and Cabinet minister, brings experience in public service and the coffee sector, having served on the Senate Committee on Agriculture. He has supported reforms to improve farmer earnings and cooperative marketing.

Henry Kinyua was appointed Chairperson of the Coffee Research and Training Institute for three years, effective October 30. The new institutions aim to increase annual coffee production to 150,000 metric tonnes, from a projected 60,000 tonnes in the 2025/2026 season, by improving varieties and farmer training.

za.headline: Zille highlights Joburg water crisis on election day
za.dek: DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille stated that 50 suburbs have been without water, calling it the city's most urgent challenge.
paragraphs: Johannesburg's severe water crisis became a central issue on election day, with DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille highlighting the desperation of residents in dozens of suburbs facing repeated outages. Millions of South Africans voted on Wednesday amidst a deepening service delivery crisis, including a reported R220 billion infrastructure backlog and failing municipal services. Zille, casting her ballot at Emmarentia Primary School, declared the water crisis the most urgent challenge facing Johannesburg.

Zille stated that 50 suburbs had no water over the past weekend, describing it as a major crisis for a city of Johannesburg's size. She noted that the outages disproportionately affect residents who cannot afford alternatives, making the desperation palpable. Zille acknowledged expectations for immediate action but warned that years of neglect have created a long-term infrastructure crisis requiring emergency short-term solutions and medium-to-long-term infrastructure fixes.

Beyond service delivery, Zille drew a line on coalition politics, stating the DA would not enter unstable governing arrangements dependent on the EFF, preferring opposition to unworkable coalitions. She argued that political instability significantly contributed to Johannesburg’s decline, emphasizing the need for stable government to reverse deterioration. Zille reserved strong criticism for the ANC, blaming its governance failures for the collapse of state and municipal entities.

za.headline: South Africa faces severe thunderstorms and high fire danger
za.dek: Yellow Level 4 warnings issued for Gauteng, Mpumalanga, Limpopo, Free State, North West, and KwaZulu-Natal, with extreme fire conditions in the Northern Cape and Eastern Cape.
paragraphs: South Africa is bracing for severe weather on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with widespread thunderstorms, heavy rain, and hail expected in several provinces. A yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms, bringing flooding and property damage, covers Gauteng, Mpumalanga Highveld, central-southern Limpopo, eastern Free State and North West, and most of KwaZulu-Natal. These storms may cause localized power and communication disruptions.

Extreme fire danger conditions are forecast for the Northern Cape, most of the Eastern Cape interior, and parts of the Western Cape, Free State, North West, Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. The South African Weather Service has issued a Red Level 10 warning for veld fires in areas including Molteno, Queenstown, and Grahamstown, advising the public against starting fires due to risks of property damage, loss of grazing, and potential loss of life.

Specific storm warnings are in place for areas like Rustenburg, Frankfort, Hartebeespoort, and Reitz, with storms expected between 13:00 and 23:59. Meanwhile, Musina, Kimberley, and Mthatha are predicted to be the hottest cities, reaching 38°C. The weather service also noted very high UVB sunburn index levels for Gauteng, advising precautions against sun exposure.

za.headline: South Africa petrol price drops by 1 cent
za.dek: Diesel prices fall by up to R1.20 per litre following government fuel levy adjustments.
paragraphs: South African motorists will pay less for fuel from Wednesday, November 4, 2026, after petrol prices decreased by 1 cent per litre. Diesel prices saw more significant reductions, with 0.05% sulphur diesel falling by R1.10 per litre and 0.005% sulphur diesel dropping by R1.20 per litre. Wholesale illuminating paraffin, however, increased by R2.75 per litre.

These changes follow the National Treasury's announcement of a R10 billion fuel relief package, which included a temporary reduction of R1.50 per litre for petrol and R3.00 per litre for diesel. This intervention was introduced after motorists faced potential substantial price hikes due to deteriorating fuel recoveries in October. The slate levy increase largely negated the petrol levy reduction.

The inland price for Petrol 95 is now R30.24 per litre, down from R30.25 in October, while coastal Petrol 95 is R29.37, down from R29.38. Inland Diesel 0.005% is R31.60, down from R32.80. The Brent crude oil price is $102.18 a barrel, and the rand/dollar exchange rate is R16.44/$.

za.headline: Activist walks SA to protest farm attacks
za.dek: Petrus Sitho left a job in 2018 to speak out about farm murders and has walked hundreds of kilometres.
paragraphs: Activist Petrus Sitho has walked hundreds of kilometres across South Africa to protest farm attacks, including a 129km walk from Frankfort to Memel in the Free State. Sitho left a well-paid job in 2018, feeling called to speak out about farm murders after growing up on a farm in Bultfontein. He has described himself on Facebook as a digital creator aiming to make a difference.

Sitho’s activism intensified after he was dismissed from his job in 2020 for travelling to Senekal to support farmers following the murder of Brendin Horner. He has interviewed survivors and claims to be the first activist to travel around South Africa interviewing farmers and farm workers. Sitho has also stated he was the first activist to debate a petition on farm killings in Parliament.

The activist's campaigns have led to death threats and an assault outside the Union Buildings in 2018. Sitho has openly criticised the government, writing an open letter to President Cyril Ramaphosa stating he does not believe the president cares about farm killings. He recently asked the public to fund a trip to the United States to present his cause to US President Donald Trump.
za.body:

Sitho left a well-paid job in 2018, feeling called to speak out about farm murders after growing up on a farm in Bultfontein. He has described himself on Facebook as a digital creator aiming to make a difference.

Sitho’s activism intensified after he was dismissed from his job in 2020 for travelling to Senekal to support farmers following the murder of Brendin Horner. He has interviewed survivors and claims to be the first activist to travel around South Africa interviewing farmers and farm workers. Sitho has also stated he was the first activist to debate a petition on farm killings in Parliament.

The activist's campaigns have led to death threats and an assault outside the Union Buildings in 2018. ng.headline: Peter Obi visit prompts Bayelsa political shifts
ng.dek: Ijaw leaders demand development and unity following the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate's visit.
paragraphs: Presidential candidate Peter Obi's recent visit to Bayelsa State has triggered a political realignment, with Ijaw leaders calling for development and unity. The visit, which coincided with Senator Henry Seriake Dickson's homecoming as National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), included the commissioning of the NDC state secretariat in Yenagoa and political engagements.

Professor Benjamin Okaba, former President of the Ijaw National Congress, stated that Obi's visit introduced a significant new dimension to Bayelsa politics and the wider Ijaw Nation. He noted that Senator Dickson's experience as a former governor and senator provides the NDC with an important political foothold in the state.

Okaba emphasized that cultural celebrations, like the traditional Ijaw war canoe and boat regatta at Toru-Orua, must be accompanied by a sustained commitment to the welfare and development of riverine communities. He also highlighted Obi's comments on the marginalisation of oil-producing communities.

ng.headline: Nigeria adopts SOP to boost food systems
ng.dek: The unified procedure aims to improve coordination and policy implementation across the agricultural value chain by 2030.
paragraphs: Nigeria's Food Systems Technical Committee has adopted a unified Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to strengthen coordination and ensure effective policy implementation across the country’s agricultural value chain. This initiative aims to guarantee nutrition security by 2030, addressing challenges like low productivity, high food prices, and post-harvest losses.

The SOP will provide clear guidance for actors from production to processing, helping stakeholders understand their roles for a coordinated approach to food systems transformation. Dr. Clementina Ebere-Okoro, National Convenor of the UN Food Systems Implementation Team, announced the development at the Agri-Food System Transformation and Innovation (AFTI) Programme meeting.

Former National Convenor Dr. Sanjo Faniran described the SOP adoption as a paradigm shift, noting increased state prioritization of agro-processing to reduce losses and maximize produce value. The initiative also seeks to boost local food production, make nutritious food affordable, create jobs, and improve farmers’ incomes.

ng.headline: Naira trades at ₦1,347.30 in official market
ng.dek: The naira weakened for a second consecutive trading session, closing at N1,348 per dollar on Wednesday.
paragraphs: The naira traded at different rates against the US dollar on Thursday, November 5, 2026. In the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the dollar was valued at approximately ₦1,347.30. At the parallel market, Bureau De Change operators bought the dollar at approximately ₦1,380 and sold it at ₦1,390.

The figures show Nigerians buying dollars through the parallel market paid more than those accessing foreign exchange officially. The difference between the official rate and the parallel market selling rate was approximately ₦42.70 per dollar. Exchange rates fluctuate based on dollar supply, demand, market liquidity, and trading activities.

The naira weakened for a second consecutive trading session in November, closing at N1,348 per dollar on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, compared with N1,347.75/$ recorded on Tuesday. Nigerians seeking foreign exchange for international travel, school fees, business transactions and other payments are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed Bureau De Change operators.

ng.headline: Kano state to irrigate 2,000 acres for farming
ng.dek: 11 new mini dams will expand year-round cultivation, boosting farmer productivity and rural incomes.
paragraphs: The Kano State Government plans to develop 11 mini dams to bring an additional 2,000 acres of farmland under irrigation for year-round production. Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr. Danjuma Mahmoud, stated this aims to increase cultivable land and improve farmer productivity. The government has already restored over 1,200 acres by rehabilitating irrigation facilities at Jermambaka, Kadawa, and Bunkure A and B.

A further 200 acres were recovered through a partnership with the Federal Government and the ATAPS project. The state is also developing an irrigation facility at Donsushiya, comprising a two-kilometre dam with a three billion cubic litre capacity, designed to serve 500 hectares. This project is 40 per cent complete, with its 14-kilometre access road finished.

The proposed mini dams will be located in Bebeji, Kibiya, Sumaila, Doguwa, Shanono, Dawakin Kudu, Gaya, Rogo, Dala, Dawakin Tofa, and Ungogo local government areas. Compensation has been paid in at least six locations, and contractors are mobilised to some sites, including Bebeji. The expanded irrigation network is expected to generate employment and discourage rural migration.

et.headline: 48 killed in Oromia armed attack, rights commission confirms
et.dek: The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission reported 20 injured, 247 households displaced, and 21 houses destroyed in Southeast Oromia.
paragraphs: The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission (EHRC) confirmed 48 people died and 20 were injured in an armed attack on October 24, 2026, in Southeast Oromia Zone. The Oromo Liberation Front, known as OLF-Shene, reportedly attacked Birbona Chole Kebele between 6:30 a.m. and 8:30 p.m., destroying 21 houses and displacing 247 households.

Victims included 23 security personnel, five militia members, and 20 civilians, according to the EHRC report which gathered information from witnesses and officials. EHRC Chief Commissioner Berhanu Adelo called the incident extremely serious and urged the government to strengthen civilian protection and improve early warning systems.

The commission has repeatedly called for government action to prevent similar attacks in the former Arsi Zone and stressed the state's constitutional duty to protect citizens' rights. The EHRC is continuing investigations into other human rights violations across the Southeast Oromia Zone and other regions.

et.headline: AU renews Ethiopia-Eritrea peace talks
et.dek: Ambassador Bankole Adeoye calls for implementation of Algiers and Pretoria agreements to prevent crisis.
paragraphs: The African Union has restarted diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea. Ambassador Bankole Adeoye, AU Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security, stated the AU is engaging leaders in both nations to prevent a full-blown crisis in the Horn of Africa.

Adeoye confirmed the AU is working to re-energize the Algiers Agreement between Ethiopia and Eritrea, and the Pretoria Agreement that ended the Tigray conflict. He said former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta is conducting consultations as the AU Chairperson’s High Representative for the Horn of Africa.

The AU Commission will continue engaging all parties to prevent the situation from escalating, Adeoye said, emphasizing collective security and condemning external interference. He noted that African leaders adopted new mechanisms in Luanda in August 2026 to improve conflict prevention and identify emerging threats.

et.headline: Ethiopia and DHL boost coffee export capacity
et.dek: A new deal will train exporters in international trade, logistics, and customs procedures.
paragraphs: The Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Authority (ECTA) and DHL Express Ethiopia signed a deal on November 3 to improve coffee export capacity. The partnership, part of DHL’s GoTrade programme, aims to enhance knowledge of international trade, logistics, and customs for Ethiopian coffee businesses.

ECTA Director Office head Sefissa Ababu stated the agreement will equip enterprises with skills for international markets, improving competitiveness and value addition. DHL Express Ethiopia Commercial Manager Yonas Sbhat noted that while demand for Ethiopian coffee is strong, customs and logistics can be barriers, especially for growing businesses.

The cooperation has already supported a nine-month training program for about 30 participants from private coffee firms and ECTA. The United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) facilitated the MoU through its ACT Coffee Programme.

et.headline: Tigray rebels claim heavy army losses
et.dek: The Tigray People's Liberation Front said it killed 500 soldiers and wounded 800 more in clashes near Aksum.
paragraphs: Ethiopia's Tigray rebels claimed on Monday to have killed 500 soldiers and wounded 800 others in clashes with government forces and allied militias. The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) said the fighting occurred on Saturday near Aksum, a historic town in the northern region.

According to TPLF-affiliated Dimtsi Weyane television, the rebels also captured territory and seized weapons, ammunition, food, and medical supplies. The group accused federal forces of using artillery and drones, and reported disruptions to telephone and internet services in the area. Ethiopia's government has not commented on the casualty figures, which could not be independently verified.

These clashes follow weeks of escalating fighting in northern Ethiopia. Government troops had captured several towns, including Mekelle, the Tigray regional capital, in early October, but TPLF fighters have continued counterattacks.

gh.headline: Ghana to build 21,000-tonne grain storage facility
gh.dek: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture signed an MoU with DMT Collateral Management for the facility in Wa, Upper West Region.
paragraphs: Ghana will soon have a 21,000-metric-tonne grain storage facility in the Upper West Region following a Memorandum of Understanding signed between the Ministry of Food and Agriculture and DMT Collateral Management. The project, scheduled for completion by August 2027, aims to reduce post-harvest losses and bolster national food security by constructing silos in Wa.

The facility will serve as a food security hub and an emergency reserve, described as a "hospital bin" for food supplies during crises, according to DMT Collateral Managing Director Paul Minlah. The project involves a €4.8 million export credit facility and an additional US$5 million investment, with DMT Collateral managing technical development and financing. Local capacity will be built through training for National Service personnel and Ghanaian technicians.

Minister of Food and Agriculture Eric Opoku stated the facility addresses inadequate storage infrastructure despite increased rice and maize production, which strains the National Food Buffer Stock Company's capacity. This Wa project is the first phase of a national expansion, with 15 to 20 similar facilities potentially planned across the country. Omanbapa AgriTech Limited also presented publicity materials for the upcoming 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration.

gh.headline: Ghana chamber seeks industry-wide financing collaboration
gh.dek: The Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy is pushing for joint efforts to overcome funding hurdles in the electric two-wheeler sector.
paragraphs: The Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy (GCCE) is calling for increased collaboration between government, financial institutions, and industry players to address financing challenges in Ghana's electric two-wheeler sector. Ms. Emmanuella Biney, GCCE Programmes and Outreach Manager, stated that solving these constraints requires more than just capital, but also suitable financing structures, stronger institutional ties, and supportive policies to boost investor confidence.

Ms. Biney made these remarks at a stakeholder workshop in Accra on Tuesday, organized by the GCCE and the William Davidson Institute at the University of Michigan. The event gathered manufacturers, assemblers, retailers, and financial institutions to discuss funding barriers and explore policy solutions. Ms. Biney emphasized that no single entity can solve these issues, necessitating coordinated action.

The workshop identified seven preliminary financing gaps, including the limited implementation of import duty waivers for electric two-wheeler companies and difficulties in securing follow-on investment after grant funding. Other issues highlighted were limited access to affordable local-currency debt and an information gap between companies and capital providers. Findings will inform a joint GCCE and WDI report to guide policy and financing measures for electric mobility businesses.

gh.headline: Mahama defends speed cameras after child deaths
gh.dek: President Mahama says Ghana cannot delay stricter traffic enforcement as children continue to die on roads.
paragraphs: President John Dramani Mahama defended the TraffiTech-GH speed enforcement system, stating that the deaths and injuries of schoolchildren hit by speeding vehicles made stricter traffic regulation necessary. He said Ghana could not afford to delay measures to control speeding while children were losing their lives or suffering permanent disabilities on their way from school. The president stressed that protecting vulnerable road users, especially schoolchildren, must be a priority in the nation's efforts to reduce road crashes.

Speaking at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, President Mahama argued that protecting lives justified using technology for traffic enforcement. He rejected public concerns about penalty costs and road conditions, stating that road maintenance and traffic law enforcement were not mutually exclusive. He cited the United Kingdom, where speed cameras operate despite imperfect roads, to support his view that enforcement should not wait for all infrastructure issues to be resolved.

Road safety statistics show Ghana recorded 2,949 road crash deaths in 2025, an 18.2 per cent increase from 2,494 in 2024. The crashes also caused 16,714 injuries, and pedestrian knockdowns rose by seven per cent to 2,561 cases. President Mahama stated that controlling excessive speed is an immediate road safety intervention, particularly in areas with many pedestrians and children.

gh.headline: Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago explore joint reparatory justice mechanism
gh.dek: Ministers discussed a dedicated platform, potentially co-chaired by AU and CARICOM, for engagement with the UK.
paragraphs: Ghana and Trinidad and Tobago are exploring a joint mechanism to advance reparatory justice and engage with the United Kingdom. The proposal emerged from a bilateral meeting between Ghana's Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and his Trinidad and Tobago counterpart Sean S.M. Sobers during the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda.

The ministers agreed that existing platforms like the Commonwealth Foreign Affairs Ministers Meeting are too broad for focused reparatory justice discussions. They stressed the need for a dedicated platform to coordinate engagement with the UK and other international partners, emphasizing that reparatory justice should encompass acknowledgement, reconciliation, and non-repetition, not just financial compensation.

Trinidad and Tobago proposed development-focused interventions such as scholarships, healthcare infrastructure support, and educational improvements as part of the reparatory process. Climate cooperation was also identified as a potential area. This initiative follows Ghana's diplomatic success in March 2026 when the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution A/RES/80/250, recognizing the enslavement of Africans as a grave crime against humanity.

cd.headline: DR Congo justice agents protest unpaid bonuses
cd.dek: Over 100 ministry staff blocked roads and burned tires in Kinshasa demanding their permanent bonuses.
paragraphs: Over 100 agents from the Ministry of Justice in Kinshasa protested on Tuesday, November 3, demanding payment of their permanent bonuses. The agents blocked roads and burned tires in front of the Ministry of Public Service, disrupting activities in the area. Police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.

The protesters stated their action began the previous day at the Ministry of Finance. They claim to have only received a portion of their bonuses, covering the first quarter, and are protesting an administrative blockage preventing the release of the remaining funds. One agent declared they were demanding their rights to bonuses that already exist within their budget.

The agents believe the non-payment of these bonuses further deteriorates their living conditions and contradicts the social policy promoted by the head of state. Officials from the Ministries of Finance and Public Service had not yet responded to requests for comment at the time of reporting.

cd.headline: Fire disrupts Kinshasa medical Centre
cd.dek: Emergency services evacuated patients from Centre Médical Diamant after a generator fire on November 4.
paragraphs: A fire disrupted patient care on Wednesday, November 4, at the Centre Médical Diamant in Kinshasa's Ngaliema commune. The blaze, which started around 6 a.m., forced staff to urgently evacuate patients, including those in intensive care.

The medical facility showed signs of damage, with broken windows from the flames. Medical teams worked outside to manage the aftermath, while thick smoke rose into the sky hours after firefighters from the Kinshasa City Hall and MONUSCO controlled the fire. Consultations were temporarily stopped.

Witnesses suggested a generator left running in the scanner room, at the moment the national electricity company (SNEL) restored power, may have caused the fire, though official confirmation is pending. No injuries or deaths were reported due to the rapid evacuation and emergency response.

tz.headline: Tanzania opposition party mourns 500 killed in 2025 election crisis
tz.dek: CHADEMA held a memorial event in Dar es Salaam for victims of the violence that followed the October 29, 2025, elections.
paragraphs: Tanzania's opposition party, CHADEMA, held a national memorial event on November 3, 2026, in Dar es Salaam to remember over 500 people killed during the 2025 election crisis. The party announced a seven-day mourning period, flying flags at half-mast. The ceremony included prayers, poetry, candle lighting, and laying flowers.

Party communications personnel Brenda Rupia read a message stating, “The lives of our loved ones were of great value.” The message honored those lost and affirmed the party's commitment to truth, dignity, and justice. Vice Chairperson John Heche addressed the difficult historical period and claims of leadership blame for the crisis.

A Commission of Inquiry, chaired by retired Chief Justice Mohamed Chande Othman, investigated the violence and presented findings on April 23, 2026. The commission reported 518 deaths and 2,390 injuries, with evidence suggesting planned and coordinated execution by organised groups motivated by grievances or financial promises.

tz.headline: Tanzania seeks AfDB funding for new power line
tz.dek: The government discussed financing for a 400kV transmission line from Kisongo to Segera with the African Development Bank.
paragraphs: The Tanzanian government, through the Ministry of Energy and TANESCO, met with the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Dodoma to discuss financing for energy projects. Key among these is a proposed 400-kilovolt (400kV) power transmission line stretching from Kisongo through Same to Segera.

Commissioner for Electricity and Renewable Energy, Engineer Innocent Luoga, chaired the talks, emphasizing the need to expand transmission infrastructure to meet rising energy demand. The project aims to strengthen the national power system, increase transmission capacity, and ensure reliable electricity for homes and businesses, particularly in Arusha and Tanga regions.

Discussions also covered expanding the Lemugur power substation in Arusha and building new substations in Same and Segera. The meeting explored financing arrangements and implementation preparations for these initiatives.

tz.headline: MPs ask Tanzania to guarantee Lissu fair trial
tz.dek: Lawmakers from six countries and the EU urged President Hassan to rule out the death penalty for Tundu Lissu.
paragraphs: 23 parliamentarians from six countries and the European Union have asked Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan to guarantee a fair trial for CHADEMA chairperson Tundu Lissu and rule out the death penalty. The appeal, published by British MP Alicia Kearns on November 3, comes ahead of the High Court's treason verdict scheduled for Friday, November 6, 2026.

The lawmakers' letter, dated November 2, seeks assurances for Lissu and protection for peaceful political opposition, stating that political disagreement should not be criminalised. Dar es Salaam police, however, warned on November 3 of alleged plans for disorder on judgement day, as they monitor reports of mobilisation for court attendance. Lissu’s family is preparing to attend court before travelling to Arusha for his elder brother's funeral.

The appeal references a February finding by the UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention that Lissu’s detention was arbitrary and calls for his release. It also cites a July recommendation from the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group for his detention to be resolved within 30 days, a deadline that has passed. President Hassan, on November 2, instructed the human-rights commission to respond to foreign allegations while investigating domestic conditions.
